ModuleName: Accessibility Standards and Inclusive Interface Design
CourseName: CEN3722 - Introduction to Human Computer Interfaces

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: A structured outline of the module's learning topics—covering WCAG guidelines and POUR principles, accessible color and visual design, keyboard navigation, and screen reader compatibility—used by learners to preview what the module covers and by instructors to verify curriculum scope.

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics (HTML)
Artifacts.Description: An HTML overview page listing the module's topics—including WCAG foundations, guideline structure, and the rationale for accessibility standards—that learners use to navigate the scope of the module and instructors use to see what content areas are covered.

Artifacts.Name: Foundations of WCAG Guidelines
Artifacts.Description: This reading introduces the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) as the foundational framework for digital accessibility, covering its structure, principles, and role in shaping design decisions from the start of a project; learners use it to build conceptual grounding before studying specific accessibility requirements.

Artifacts.Name: Accessible Color and Visual Design
Artifacts.Description: This reading explains how to apply color and visual design choices accessibly, covering contrast ratios, color blindness considerations, low vision accommodations, and cognitive accessibility; learners and instructors use it to understand how visual presentation can either barrier or support diverse users.

Artifacts.Name: Keyboard Navigation and Motor Accessibility
Artifacts.Description: This reading covers keyboard navigation as a core accessibility requirement, explaining how users with motor disabilities rely on keyboard-only interaction and what designers must do to ensure full keyboard operability; learners use it to understand focus management, tab order, and motor-accessible interface patterns.

Artifacts.Name: Screen Reader Compatibility
Artifacts.Description: This reading explains how screen readers work and how web content must be structured—using semantic HTML, ARIA roles, and proper labeling—to be interpreted correctly by assistive technologies; learners use it to design and evaluate interfaces that are operable for blind and low-vision users.

Artifacts.Name: Inclusive Design Principles Beyond WCAG
Artifacts.Description: This reading presents inclusive design as a philosophy that extends beyond WCAG compliance, exploring how designing for the full spectrum of human diversity benefits all users; learners use it to shift their perspective from checkbox accessibility toward proactive, human-centered design thinking.

Artifacts.Name: Accessibility Auditing
Artifacts.Description: This reading describes the process of conducting an accessibility audit against WCAG standards, covering evaluation methods, tools, and how to systematically identify barriers in a digital interface; instructors and learners use it to understand how to assess real products for accessibility compliance and usability gaps.

Artifacts.Name: Applying Corrective Design Patterns
Artifacts.Description: This reading details corrective design patterns used to remediate accessibility barriers identified in audits, emphasizing structural and behavioral component-level fixes rather than superficial patches; learners use it to learn how to redesign components correctly after an audit reveals problems.
